executiveVerdict.summary: You score 37/100 (Weak), needing 38 more points to reach a competitive band. Your CV & application score of 11/30 is the single largest drag: every bullet uses passive, task-level language with no stated finding, output or impact. Your ATS score of 7/10 is the strongest component but is undermined by zero role-relevant keywords. Competency evidence is thin across all seven dimensions, and your technical gaps — six missed quiz concepts — leave the numerical and commercial sections well below competitive. The CV is repairable, but all three areas need work before you submit.
executiveVerdict.mostImportantFix: Rewrite every CV bullet to include a specific action and a stated output or finding. This directly lifts your lowest-scoring component (CV & application 11/30) and gives competency answers real evidence to draw on.
executiveVerdict.submitAdvice: Do not submit until you have: (1) rewritten your CV bullets with specific outputs, (2) drilled all six missed technical concepts, and (3) prepared at least one concrete commercial observation from your business-news reading. Check the official vacancy for eligibility, deadlines and application limits — none of those are confirmed here.

competencyRepair.answerStructure: Situation: essay task at Loughborough. Action: compared techniques, evaluated library sources. Result: produced a structured argument. Reflection: what this shows about how you approach evidence.
competencyRepair.draftAnswer: In my first term at Loughborough, I was set an essay that required me to compare narrative techniques across two novels. Rather than just summarising the texts, I went to the library and found sources that had analysed similar techniques, then used those to build my own argument about what the comparison revealed. [confirm: what were the two novels and the techniques you compared?] I had to decide which sources were most relevant and how to weave them into a coherent line of reasoning rather than just listing views. [confirm: what did your essay argue or conclude?] The process taught me that analysis means taking a position and defending it with evidence, not just describing what you found. [confirm: what grade or feedback did you receive, if any?]
